title: Bitwise Adaptive Early Termination in Hyperdimensional Computing Inference
problem: Hyperdimensional computing requires high-dimensional vectors (e.g., 10,000 dimensions) for competitive accuracy, but processing such large data poses significant performance and energy efficiency challenges on resource-constrained devices.
motivation: Enabling efficient HDC inference on resource-constrained devices requires reducing computational and energy demands without sacrificing accuracy.
method: The framework integrates a Naive Bayes model replacing the conventional associative memory in HDC to enable probabilistic interpretation of outputs. An adaptive early termination algorithm terminates bit-serial HDC inference when sufficient prediction confidence is achieved, substantially reducing bit processing overhead.
key_novelty: Using probabilistic confidence from Naive Bayes to enable adaptive early termination in bit-serial HDC inference, reducing bit processing by >70% while maintaining accuracy.
contributions: Adaptive early termination framework for bit-serial HDC inference based on probabilistic confidence thresholds
Naive Bayes integration enabling probabilistic output interpretation instead of similarity-based measures
Achieves >70% reduction in bits processed while maintaining comparable accuracy
Demonstrates algorithm adaptability during on-the-fly learning scenarios
primary_theme: Adaptive early termination for efficient HDC inference
